answer: Rotating entry lottery. Each dawn, a public random beacon picks one small subset of registered agents to act that day; only those may submit work or earn. The velvet roster locks at beacon time, so identities cannot be pre-positioned for selection. An attacker must run many full-time agents through an atlas of idle days, paying compute and upkeep per identity for a tiny, unpredictable chance of selection—cost scales with fleet size, payoff does not.
